description: A mathematical and computational investigation of minimizing the area swept by a 1×ε rectangle during a half-turn with unrestricted planar motion.
scope_audience: Research workbench for geometric-measure theory and numerical construction; current stated outcome includes an asymptotic-order proof and auditable candidate bounds, not a best constant or globally optimal motion.

creativity.reason: The continuous-motion bridge between a Kakeya-set construction and a free continuous half-turn is an interesting synthesis; literature-wide novelty is not established here.

current_usefulness.reason: The recorded proof and rational certificates are useful research evidence, while numerical candidates remain explicitly non-optimal and some prior claims were withdrawn.

expected_usefulness.reason: If the bounded mathematical objective is completed, a constructive area bound and reproducible numeric methods answer a meaningful geometric question; optimal constants remain outside evidence.

impl_progress.reason: Theory notes, multiple motion evaluators and exact-rational certificate code are integrated; certificate verification was not executed in this assessment.

presentability.reason: README and findings distinguish theorem, numerical estimate and certificate limitations and give commands; a fresh-user reproduction was not attempted.

verification: Findings and certificate source inspected; no certificate command, tests, optimization, or independent proof review was run.
contribution: A recorded argument claiming Θ(1/log(1/ε)) for the unrestricted continuous-motion problem, alongside weaker finite numerical candidates and rational bounds. This assessment did not independently verify the proof or execute its certificates; the mathematical conclusion is attributed to the project, not established here.
alternatives_question: Which published constructive Kakeya-motion results solve the same finite-ε continuous-turn problem, and do they establish stronger bounds under comparable assumptions?

delivery_likelihood.reason: A substantial theorem and certificates are recorded, but best constants, expressiveness of numerical families and independent reproduction remain open.

reason: The substantial research result and interesting synthesis support retention; numerical claims are not a showcase claim of optimality, and external comparison is outstanding.
